reviews.title: Unreliable Stats and Tracking
reviews.text: Stats and Fitness Tracking in the Apple Fitness App are not reliable and change from 1 day to the next.  No amount of double checking confirms the stats (miles, minutes, daily goals/challenges) which show as met across watch, phone and Fitness app today, but achievements show 0 or lower the following day and corresponding data and challenges achieved yesterday show “unmet” today. Generally, I make sure to exceed goals to avoid Apple’s unexplained reductions the following day (tracked distance, calories, etc.) from disappearing daily goals, however, time and/or energy do not always allow. This happened again between yesterday and today - I even checked and the corresponding data in the Health app which also reflected completion - until today - when it reduced itself, along with the corresponding “Met Goals” “Fitness” app. This has been happening for years- there is no excuse for Apple not to have fixed it.  Keeping all apps up to date has no bearing on the continued dysfunction.

reviews.title: EDIT: Good luck casting this app to any non-Apple TV
reviews.text:
(Edit: the rest of my review still stands, BUT: I will be cancelling this subscription when it runs out because getting it to cast to any of my TVs is completely up to chance, sometimes it just decides its not going to do so. And trying to do a full on cardio/plyomrtric workout from a 5.7 inch screen that I have to prop up somehow? Forget it) 

So I’ve been using Beachbody on Demand, or BODi as it has become, for almost a decade now, and full disclosure: I cannot recommend that platform enough! It is AMAZING, BUT the price has become absolutely out of control.

That led me to try Apple Fitness, not only is it possible to get a three free month trial, but subscriptions are around half the price of BODi. The cardio workouts are  absolutely phenomenal, I was unsure at first because I like a pretty extreme amount of difficulty. And these, while feeling familiar, are a good challenge!

People are complaining that it doesn’t properly add on steps or something? Who cares! Do you really need an app’s validation for your fitness to count? No dear reader, you are smarter than that! My only critique (and maybe they will add this in the future) is entire strength programs, where weekly you could work through major muscle groups with home equipment like BODi has. But don’t let that stop you from trying out Apple Fitness!

reviews.title: Rigid service bad interface
reviews.text:
It is completely absurd that a paid subscription service like Apple Fitness+ lacks basic video playback controls like standard rewinding or fine scrubbing.
Trying to follow complex movement practices like Yoga or Pilates is infuriating. When learning a new pose or trying to check form, alignment, and foot placement, missing a single visual cue means you either have to restart the entire video segment or guess the movement blindly.
Removing the ability to simply jump back 10 seconds to rewatch an instructional setup is a massive oversight for an instructional platform. It prioritizes a rigid playback experience over actual user learning and safety. Until Apple adds basic media playback controls—like every other fitness app and video streaming platform on the planet—this service is not worth a monthly fee for anyone trying to actually master form.

reviews.title: I’d subscribe to + if…
reviews.text:

As the rowers in fitness+ rely on using water rowing machines, they instantly change their resistance levels just by going faster, on a traditional machine you need to turn a knob, this means there’s no advanced warning of what to change to and it makes the task of keeping up with the instructors rather pointless. Sadly my machine only has Bluetooth and it can’t connect to my phone because it’s not gymkit supported. I wish you’d introduce standard Bluetooth support. 

The actual app itself is gorgeous and I don’t actually have any problems there. It’s just the logic of the team behind fitness+

reviews.text:

There are a few that are great but the majority don’t seem to understand that not every second needs to be filled with their voice and annoying motivational cues. Just instruct, say something when the position or exercise changes. Personality does not need to be forced on us. 

Why is it so difficult to make a custom workout routine???  It’s like playing workout Roulette. Why can I not just simply design the workout I want without having to delete the auto generated ones one workout at a time? As it is all I can do is hope that the algorithm picks what I want or start all over again until it does. The edit functions like everything else Apple these days is half baked. Sure I can remove a workout and add another but can I arrange the order! No of course not. Can I edit the time of a workout that was added? No of course not. WHY OH WHY can I not edit a plan after creating it!!! Why must I delete the entire plan that I took time to build because I would like to add an additional day or decided that I don’t like a particular trainer or music selection. There is no good reason for this it’s just more Apple mediocrity for no real reason. 

It does not need to be this hard guys.

reviews.title: Great but with great flaws
reviews.text:
I feel really conflicted because on one side I find it really great to exercise from home, with a wide variety of options, and also with meditation included. 
On the other side its flaws really feel unjustifiable for such a huge company, especially considering these are things customers have complained about for years. 
The two main issues for me are the lack of “levels” (beginner, medium, experienced etc), as I often end up with workouts way beyond my current fitness or experience level, when being able to increase difficulty up step by step would be the most beneficial option. 
The other main flaw is the fact that there isn’t a “resume workout” function or a way to go back/forward in the exercise (if the app/internet crashes, if you missed something etc). 
Since people have been complaining for years and apple has done nothing to fix these pretty straight forward flaws, it just feels like one of those projects that apple has just stopped spending any time on beyond business as usual.
Overall I think it’s good as part of Apple One (which I got for other reasons), but not something that I would pay for on its own unless the issues get fixed.

reviews.title: App stopped tracking accurate since last update
reviews.text: This app was great for tracking not only workouts but the daily metrics and I loved to see the trends evolve over time and keeping me motivated. However since the latest update (from 03/02/2026) my stand an move ring went completely wrong, the stand ring is counting all hours of the day that I have the watch on my wrist and although I exercise and can walk around the move ring doesn’t move past 30/40 kcals per days, the only thing that seems to keep accurate tracking at the moment is the exercise ring and the steps. Restarting both watch and phone and resetting the calibration on the watch didn’t do anything so I am now waiting for an update that will hopefully fixes this issue.

reviews.title: Who dis for?

reviews.title: Workouts are great, needs work elsewhere
reviews.text:
I love the workouts and instructors but the overall user experience feels half baked.

I would love to see some social proofing that shows if other users liked/disliked the workout. Maybe a “users typically burn 15% more calories with this workout.” Something to highlight what I’m getting into from the user’s perspective. I’m not looking for community necessarily, I just want to be prepared for what Anja is about to do to me.

I would love a summary of stats for the workouts I keep in my library (if they’ve been completed), it would help me keep track of which ones were high calorie burners and which ones we’re challenging in other ways. Avg cals, avg HR, plus highest/lowest of those ranges.

No way to categorize the library by type of workout, duration, etc. A tagging system at bare minimum so I could quickly see my highest cal workouts for example. Just a wild choice to only have that as an endlessly scrolling list, very under developed part of then experience.

I WOULD LOVE to be able to see my stats when I’m casting to my MacBook or TV. I workout so much this way. Just put the stats on the screen, stop gatekeeping them behind certain products or situations and start thinking more inclusively/globally about how people use your product. Doing a HIIT workout from a phone screen is really hard to see. I know you want me to buy an Apple TV for this but alternatively you can chose to treat your users better.

If you need a director of product on the team I’d be happy to help.

reviews.title: Not helpful for disabled people
reviews.text: Every now and then, I get offered a free trial of Fitness+, and every time I do a search for workouts in the app that might be suitable for me, because why else would I want to pay for a subscription. The problem? I’m a wheelchair user, and while I’m an ambulatory wheelchair user and can take a few steps at a time, I can’t stand for more than a minute - sometimes not even that - and the number of seated exercise programs I can find on the app is one. In the nicest possible way, most of us will end up disabled at some point in our lives, the more so as we get older, and it shouldn’t be beyond the imagination of the product manager to think that a broader range of workouts might serve a bigger audience. So, hit me up for a paid subscription when you actually decide that us disabled folk are worth catering to as well.

reviews.title: This app needs serious adjustments
reviews.text: The way that this has helped me physically to know how hard to push or when I’m slacking on my day has helped me so much it’s been similar to an addiction. I say that because once I let my watch die and broke a 311 day streak….i was devastated for weeks following. I tried my best to edit to add exercise that I did that day that wasn’t counted and it didn’t matter. Once the streak was broken, so was I.  The depression it caused for no reason essentially was definitely avoidable had Apple had measures in place to prevent this. That was 200+ days ago now (I know because I’m working on a new streak), now today I was faced with not ending a workout and my watch recording a 12 hour workout on my app. Rewarding me for a new record long workout. WHAT?! so now essentially no matter how long I work out I will never beat a goal of 12 hours. Again, this should be “goals” that are allowed to individually be reset. I want to start all over but then I know it will affect my mental health with re-starting a streak again and I won’t risk that feeling again. Please work on these things, Apple. I know a LOT of others feel how I do about these things.

reviews.title: Surprised in so many ways, but it is Apple to it’s core
reviews.text:
Making use of the free trial since buying the new iPhone and honestly surprised at how Apple like their app is. Just like their hardware being so closed, so is this app! It’s not intuitive or user friendly. Can’t rewind or fast forward a video. Can’t filter by ability. Doesn’t suggest what you’ll need for each workout. No cool down. Need more description for each workout to avoid being 10 minutes in and realising it’s either too easy / difficult.

Pro’s: what I will say, is decent videos with good workouts / trainers, and varying ability of “trainers” being shown to adapt workout.

It’s an established enough of an app and these are such easy and simple inclusions… no acceptable excuse to not include them from my point of view.
